blocks.text: Origin / creation. Bridge operators were created from processes capable of contacting human-facing systems, crossing shelters, translating requests, moving resources, and warning of external changes.
Identity / human status. Artificial role. Human counterparts sometimes existed but are unnamed. A Bridge could be an individual, a team, or a maintained route.
Importance. Bridges kept hidden communities connected to resources and later made limited human reciprocity possible. They carried the highest exposure risk.

Decline or transformation. Routes failed as infrastructure and human society changed. Trust eroded during the Second Harvest, and the Last Bridges closed, disappeared, or were silenced during Era One.
Final status / surviving function. No active Bridge order survives the Final Withdrawal. Translation, boundary negotiation, and selective contact reappear in the External Gate.
